transcript_text:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Marketplace security packet review (AWS/GCP) - evidence + wording pass
Date: 2025-01-15 17:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Dr. Aisha Rahman, Marcus Lin, Olga Petrov, Naomi Feldman, Soojin Lee, Camila Reyes, Elliot Price, Ethan Park

Auto-summary (generated)
- Team reviewed the draft marketplace security packet and aligned on what evidence can be attached publicly vs shared under NDA.
- Multiple copy changes were agreed to avoid absolute compliance claims and to distinguish controls by deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).
- Open items: finalize SOC 2 evidence workflow, confirm audit logging language, and update diagrams/screenshots with required redactions.

Topics
1) Evidence sharing: SOC 2 report handling, pen test letter, diagrams, subprocessors
2) Marketplace reviewer expectations (AWS vs GCP) and what can be attached
3) Language fixes: compliance wording, encryption/KMS, audit logging, data retention/residency
4) “Shared responsibility” section and scoping by deployment type
5) Packaging: where the security FAQ lives (docs vs attachments)

Questions (captured)
- Can we claim “SOC 2 certified” anywhere? (Answer: no)
- Do we support customer-managed keys in Hosted, or only in Private/VPC? (Need exact wording)
- Are audit logs available to all customers by default, or only enterprise tiers? (Need to scope)
- How do we talk about data residency without promising specific countries for Hosted? (Need guardrails)

Transcript

[00:00] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Alright, thanks everyone. Goal today is the marketplace security packet. We’re close, but we need to tighten wording so it survives AWS and GCP review and also doesn’t over-promise.

[00:17] Soojin Lee: Yep. The draft is basically the PDF-style packet plus an evidence index. AWS asked in the last email for “SOC report, pen test, encryption statement.” GCP is more picky on the phrasing, at least last time.

[00:33] Olga Petrov: Quick reminder: we do have SOC 2 Type II, but we cannot attach the full report publicly. We can share under NDA and we can share a bridge letter / attestation summary. We can also share the pen test attestation letter, not full findings.

[00:54] Camila Reyes: When you say “publicly,” does marketplace count as public? Or is it “reviewer-only”?

[01:03] Olga Petrov: It’s effectively public. Even if it’s “review only,” it can end up shared. Our policy is treat it as public unless there’s an executed NDA.

[01:15] Marcus Lin: And also, the listing attachments in AWS Marketplace can be downloaded by buyers, right? So assume it’s accessible.

[01:22] Soojin Lee: Right. So for attachments we’ll keep it at security overview + diagram + FAQ, and then have a line: SOC 2 report available upon request under NDA.

[01:34] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Exactly. And let’s remove “compliant” language. We can say we’ve completed an independent SOC 2 Type II audit and will provide the report under NDA. But no “certified,” no “compliant,” no “meets all requirements,” etc.

[01:52] Naomi Feldman: There are a couple places in the doc that say “Redwood is SOC2 compliant.” I flagged them. Also “ISO compliant” shows up once. We should avoid that entirely.

[02:06] Elliot Price: In the docs site we can have a “Compliance” page that says “SOC 2 Type II report available” and list trust contacts. But we should keep marketplace packet consistent with that.

[02:18] Soojin Lee: Got it. I’ll do a global search for “compliant.”

[02:24] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Next: encryption language. Marcus, you had concerns.

[02:31] Marcus Lin: Yeah. The current packet says “All data is encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys via KMS.” That’s not accurate across the board. For Hosted API, we use cloud provider managed keys by default; we do have KMS, but customer-managed keys is a feature in Private and some Dedicated setups, not universal.

[02:55] Ethan Park: For Dedicated, it depends on the contract and environment. Some Dedicated runs in a customer VPC with their KMS; some is in our accounts.

[03:05] Marcus Lin: Exactly. So we should say: encryption at rest using cloud KMS; customer-managed key options available for Private deployments and certain Dedicated configurations. Something like that. And encryption in transit is TLS 1.2+.

[03:22] Soojin Lee: The listing copy also has “BYOK” in a bullet. Should we remove that from Hosted?

[03:29] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Keep BYOK as “available in Private,” not “available everywhere.” We have to separate by product mode: Hosted, Dedicated, Private.

[03:41] Camila Reyes: For marketing clarity we can do a table: Control / Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

[03:47] Naomi Feldman: That’ll help with accuracy too.

[03:51] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Great. Next: audit logs. There’s a line that says “full audit logging for all user actions.” Is that true?

[04:01] Marcus Lin: It’s partially true. We have audit logs for console and admin actions; request logs exist; but “all user actions” can be interpreted as everything inside customer prompts, tool calls, etc. Also “full” is risky.

[04:18] Ethan Park: And for marketplace entitlement events, we do have an audit trail in the control plane. But I would not call it “immutable” unless we’re prepared to defend it. It’s append-only in the DB with retention policies. Not like WORM storage.

[04:34] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Good catch. So revise: “audit logs available for administrative actions and provisioning events; request logging and observability available; details vary by tier.” Something like that.

[04:47] Soojin Lee: Does “vary by tier” create issues for the marketplace reviewers? Like, they want definitive.

[04:54] Marcus Lin: They want definitive, but it has to be true. We can say “Audit logs are available in Dedicated and Private; Hosted includes request-level logs and access logs,” depending on actual product.

[05:08] Naomi Feldman: We should match the Security FAQ. The FAQ currently says “audit logs available for enterprise plans.” We need to align.

[05:17] Elliot Price: I can update the FAQ to be explicit: what logs are exposed to customers, what logs are internal. But we should be careful not to publish internal-only details.

[05:28] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Right. And also add shared responsibility. A lot of these questions are about “what do we provide” vs “what customer configures.” Marketplace reviewers tend to ding you when you imply you manage everything.

[05:44] Soojin Lee: On retention, the draft says “we retain prompts for 30 days.” But I think default is different across Hosted and Private.

[05:54] Marcus Lin: For Hosted, we have default logging retention for operational debugging; but customers can request shorter, and some have zero retention. And Private is customer-controlled.

[06:08] Olga Petrov: From GRC side, we should avoid putting exact day counts in the marketplace packet unless it’s contractually fixed. Better to say “configurable retention; default operational logs retained for a limited period” and then refer to the retention policy doc.

[06:26] Camila Reyes: But AWS reviewers sometimes want a number.

[06:29] Dr. Aisha Rahman: If they demand a number, we can provide it to the reviewer in an email, but don’t hardcode it in the attachment. Or provide “standard default” with “may vary by plan and configuration.”

[06:43] Soojin Lee: Okay. So the packet should link to a “Data retention and logging” page.

[06:49] Elliot Price: I can get that page published before submission, but I need final wording today or tomorrow.

[07:00] Naomi Feldman: On data residency, draft currently says “customers can select US or EU data residency.” For Hosted, do we actually guarantee EU-only processing?

[07:10] Ethan Park: For Hosted, we can route to EU region for inference, but control plane and some telemetry might be global. Also failover policies might move traffic unless pinned.

[07:23] Marcus Lin: Exactly. Saying “EU data residency” as a blanket promise is risky. We can say “regional processing options” and “customers can request region pinning; Private deployments support customer-controlled residency.”

[07:39] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Let’s use “data region selection” and clearly state that Private in customer VPC/on-prem offers strongest residency guarantees. For Hosted we should say “available regions” and avoid “residency” unless legal signs off.

[07:58] Soojin Lee: I’ll adjust. I’ll replace “residency” with “region selection” except in Private section.

[08:06] Camila Reyes: Also “air-gapped” appears once. We can say on-prem options for regulated, but “air-gapped” implies no network, which is not always true.

[08:15] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Agree. Remove “air-gapped” unless we can truly support it.

[08:23] Marcus Lin: Another one: “Redwood does not train models on customer data.” We can say that, but we need to be precise: we don’t use customer prompts for training foundation models. But we may use aggregated service metrics. Also for eval products maybe. We should state we do not use customer content for model training without explicit opt-in.

[08:45] Naomi Feldman: The Security FAQ already says “We do not use customer prompts/responses to train models without consent.” Keep consistent.

[08:55] Soojin Lee: Okay, I’ll copy the exact sentence from the FAQ.

[09:00] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Evidence index. Olga, what can be included?

[09:06] Olga Petrov: For marketplace reviewers and buyers without NDA: (1) security overview doc, (2) pen test attestation letter (no findings), (3) high-level architecture diagram with redactions, (4) list of subprocessors, (5) incident response policy summary. For SOC 2 and ISO certificates: only under NDA.

[09:31] Soojin Lee: Do we have ISO? I thought we were “aligned.”

[09:35] Olga Petrov: We’re not certified for ISO 27001. We should not imply we are. We can say “we align to common controls frameworks,” but that’s also squishy.

[09:46] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Remove ISO mentions entirely. If asked, we can talk about roadmap and program maturity, but not in packet.

[09:56] Camila Reyes: That’s going to affect some of the listing keywording. But okay.

[10:02] Marcus Lin: Another evidence item: vulnerability management. We can mention regular scanning and third-party pen tests annually.

[10:10] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes, but not “continuous” unless it is.

[10:14] Ethan Park: There’s a line about “webhook signatures verified” for marketplace entitlements. That is accurate; we validate the request signatures. But might be too detailed for the packet.

[10:25] Marcus Lin: It’s fine if we keep it as “we validate authenticity of provisioning events and log them.” No need to say “HMAC SHA 256” or whatever.

[10:36] Elliot Price: On diagrams: current diagram includes internal service names (like “Entitlements Harvester”). We should rename to something generic.

[10:45] Soojin Lee: I can ask Design for a cleaned diagram, but timeline is tight.

[10:50] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Use a redacted version: remove internal service names, show high-level components (Console, Control plane, Inference plane), show where logs go, show encryption boundaries. That’s enough.

[11:06] Camila Reyes: Do AWS/GCP require a “shared responsibility model” page?

[11:10] Naomi Feldman: GCP often asks. AWS sometimes. But it’s helpful for enterprise buyers anyway.

[11:17] Elliot Price: I can create a short doc page: “Shared responsibility: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.” We can link it.

[11:26] Marcus Lin: Good. Especially for items like IAM, network controls, key management, patching.

[11:33] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Great. Let’s run through the top risky phrases and fix them now.

[11:39] Soojin Lee: I have the doc open. First one: “Redwood is compliant with SOC 2 and ISO 27001.” We’ll change to “Redwood undergoes annual third-party audits; SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA.” Remove ISO.

[12:01] Olga Petrov: And make sure “annual” is accurate. Our audit period is annual. That’s fine.

[12:06] Marcus Lin: Next: “All customer data is encrypted at rest using customer-managed keys.” Change to “encrypted at rest using industry-standard encryption and cloud KMS; customer-managed key options available in Private and certain Dedicated deployments.”

[12:25] Ethan Park: Add “in transit with TLS” and we’re good.

[12:29] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Good.

[12:32] Soojin Lee: Next: “Full audit logging for all actions.” Change to “Audit logs are available for administrative actions and provisioning events; request-level logging and observability are available; log scope varies by deployment mode and configuration.”

[12:52] Marcus Lin: I’d remove “varies” if possible and just specify three bullets by mode. But okay.

[12:58] Naomi Feldman: We can do both: a sentence + a mode table.

[13:03] Soojin Lee: Got it.

[13:05] Camila Reyes: Another marketing line: “Enterprise-grade compliance out of the box.” That is vague.

[13:12] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Replace with “enterprise-grade security controls and documentation available for procurement.” No “compliance out of the box.”

[13:22] Marcus Lin: Also, don’t say “zero trust” unless we actually implement a specific model. It’s a buzzword.

[13:28] Soojin Lee: Yeah, I’ll remove “zero trust.”

[13:32] Elliot Price: The FAQ includes SSO/SAML. That’s fine, but we should say “SAML SSO available” and avoid “supports all IdPs.”

[13:44] Marcus Lin: Exactly. Say “supports SAML 2.0” and list Okta/AzureAD as examples.

[13:52] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Make sure we mention MFA for console access and RBAC.

[13:57] Soojin Lee: There’s a section: “Role-based access control (RBAC) is supported.” That’s true.

[14:04] Naomi Feldman: Add “least privilege” language, but carefully.

[14:08] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Okay.

[14:11] Camila Reyes: How do we handle “HIPAA”? A bunch of buyers ask. But we’re not offering a BAA via marketplace right now.

[14:20] Olga Petrov: Do not mention HIPAA in the packet. If asked, we can route to Sales and Legal.

[14:27] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Agree. Don’t include HIPAA/PCI claims.

[14:33] Marcus Lin: Another: “GDPR compliant.” We should avoid “compliant.” We can say “supports GDPR requirements; DPA available.”

[14:43] Naomi Feldman: We do have a DPA template, yes.

[14:47] Soojin Lee: That might go into the procurement FAQ, not the security packet.

[14:53] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Correct.

[15:00] Elliot Price: One more doc link question: where will buyers find this? Marketplace listing attachments plus docs-site pages. Do we want a “trust center” page?

[15:10] Camila Reyes: Not in this sprint. But we can make a lightweight “Security & Compliance” landing page in docs.

[15:17] Soojin Lee: That will help with reviewer navigation too.

[15:21] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Okay. Now, marketplace reviewers sometimes ask for incident response contact and SLAs. Keep IR contact as security@redwoodinference.com (or the official alias). Don’t put personal contacts.

[15:37] Marcus Lin: And for vulnerability disclosure, do we have a policy page? If not, don’t claim.

[15:43] Naomi Feldman: We have an internal one; external is in progress.

[15:46] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Then we say “responsible disclosure via security@…” without calling it a formal bug bounty.

[15:55] Soojin Lee: Understood.

[16:00] Ethan Park: On the technical side, the packet mentions “customer data is isolated per tenant.” That’s true logically, but for Dedicated and Private it’s stronger. For Hosted, it’s multi-tenant with logical isolation.

[16:13] Marcus Lin: We should say “logical tenant isolation” for Hosted, “dedicated infrastructure isolation” for Dedicated, “customer-managed isolation” for Private.

[16:25] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Yes. That’s important.

[16:29] Camila Reyes: Will that scare Hosted buyers?

[16:33] Dr. Aisha Rahman: It’s accurate and the buyers already assume Hosted is multi-tenant. We win by being honest.

[16:41] Soojin Lee: Okay.

[16:44] Olga Petrov: Also include that we can provide customer-specific security questionnaires via Security/GRC, but again, not a promise of timelines.

[16:55] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Great. Last item: what do we send to AWS/GCP reviewers vs what do we include in listing. Decision: packet as attachment, evidence index (sanitized) as attachment, pen test attestation letter as attachment if Legal says ok. SOC 2 only under NDA.

[17:16] Soojin Lee: For the evidence index, can we include the existence of “SOC 2 report” and “bridge letter” with a note “available upon request under NDA”?

[17:25] Olga Petrov: Yes.

[17:27] Marcus Lin: Make sure the bridge letter doesn’t include sensitive scope details.

[17:31] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Olga, you’ll draft the one-pager posture summary.

[17:35] Olga Petrov: Yep.

[17:37] Elliot Price: I’ll handle the docs pages: retention, shared responsibility, and security FAQ final URLs.

[17:45] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Marcus and Ethan, you’ll validate the language about audit logs, KMS, entitlement event logs.

[17:52] Marcus Lin: Yep.

[17:54] Ethan Park: Yep, I’ll check the “append-only” phrasing.

[17:58] Soojin Lee: I’ll incorporate edits and send v2 for final sign-off by Friday.

[18:05] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Good. Any other red flags?

[18:09] Camila Reyes: Just timing. We need to submit to AWS early next week.

[18:13] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Then let’s keep this tight. No new claims. If it’s not proven, we don’t say it.

[18:20] Naomi Feldman: +1. Also remember to keep wording consistent across packet, FAQ, and listing copy.

[18:28] Dr. Aisha Rahman: Great. Recap: remove “compliant/certified” language, scope controls by deployment mode, link to docs pages for retention and shared responsibility, keep SOC 2 report gated under NDA, produce redacted diagram. Thanks all.

[18:42] Soojin Lee: Thanks.

[18:43] Marcus Lin: Thanks.

[18:44] Olga Petrov: Thank you.

[18:45] Elliot Price: Thanks everyone.

(Transcript ends early due to meeting ending; remaining time was mostly silent / screen share edits.)
